description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md part 4.  Code sha 05806e16.

REPRODUCER: scratch/s540b/rp/ppi.pl in the s540b worktree (vendor/PPI/lib + a pure-Perl Params::Util copied from s534a's scratch/s534a/ppi-lib, because the real Params::Util is XS).  Run `PCL_FASL_DEBUG=1 ./pcl ppi.pl` twice: every PPI module reports TEXT (default policy: :local) or `PPI.pm -> fasl-build` (PCL_COMPILE_DIRS='*') on the SECOND run too, and the cache entries (~/.pcl-cache/modules/<key>.lisp + .deps for PPI/Lexer.pm etc.) carry the second run's mtime -- the text is being re-transpiled, not only re-compiled.  A single local module (scratch/s540b/lm/uselocal.pl: Text::Balanced copied as My::TB) does NOT do this: its second run reuses the text (0.53 s) or the fasl (0.055 s).

WHAT THE MANIFEST SAYS: Lexer.pm's .deps lists `source local .../vendor/PPI/lib/PPI/Lexer.pm` but its 120 PPI dependencies as `installed` (and one `local`: the scratch Params::Util) -- the same files classified two ways.  The cheap discriminating measurement: diff Lexer.pm's .deps before and after one more run (scratch/s540b/nl2/: lexer-run4.deps, lexer-before.deps and the diff in legs/leg6.log) -- a line that changes names the invalidating input.  RESULT: see legs/leg6.log / the DONE note below.

WHY IT MATTERS: s534a measured "the PPI parse" at 3 s per four parses with module load EXCLUDED (Time::HiRes inside the program); the whole run of the same program is 30x that.  Any program using PPI from a source tree (a PPI checkout, a vendored copy -- PCL's own case) pays it; and the vendored PPI is the one PCL itself ships.

BAR: the second run of the reproducer reports FASL HIT / a valid text for every PPI module; module-cache guard rows (Pl/t/module-fasl-cache-01.t, cache-surface-01.t) +0.

=== RESULT (s540b leg6, 16:57) === the discriminating measurement taken: one more default-policy run rewrote PPI/Lexer.pm's cache entry (.lisp + .deps mtimes 15:33:03 -> 16:57:22) and the new .deps is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the one it replaced (the diff is empty; scratch/s540b/nl2/lexer-before.deps), the source unchanged -- so the input that invalidates the entry is NOT in the manifest's content.  What is left is an ORDERING test: the suspicion now is that p-cache-valid-p compares the entry against something rewritten in the same run (another local module's entry, or a dependency's mtime) and PPI's modules `use` each other in cycles (PPI.pm <-> PPI::Lexer / PPI::Node / PPI::Element), so each rewrite invalidates the next run's view of its neighbours.  A single local module (scratch/s540b/lm) does not show it.  Next measurement: which clause of p-cache-valid-p answers NIL for Lexer.pm on the second run (PCL_FASL_DEBUG prints only TEXT / FASL HIT today).

=== s540 (2026-11-13) === scheduled: s540/s540d-prompt.md (the USER: the speed fixing is a normal task).
subject: CACHE MISS (s540b, measured, cause NOT found): a program that `use`s the VENDORED PPI (`use lib 'vendor/PPI/lib'; use PPI;`) re-transpiles PPI's modules on EVERY run -- 98-116 s a run for two parses of Calc.pm (perl 0.4 s); with PCL_COMPILE_DIRS='*' PPI.pm is a `fasl-build` on every run and its ~100 dependencies load from TEXT
